findings.rule: specs/requests/01-requests.md requirement 35 and specs/requests/03-client-participants.md Known Gaps
findings.claim: Carried unchanged from review 2. Reassign on a client-addressed row is refused with 409 invalidTransition and the control is withheld on the detail screen — a defensible reading of spec 03's Known Gaps row and edge case 5, but a refusal no requirement states. Spec 03's Routes table does not list the reassign route at all. Not blocked: the previous pass raised the opposite direction under CR-32 and it was addressed, and re-blocking in reverse is what the closed register exists to prevent. A person should decide whether the refusal stays and, if so, write it into spec 03 with its status and message.

witness.detail: invalidTransition is scoped to "every transition route" in spec 01's error table; reassign has a section of its own documenting 200 and body validation only, and spec 03 amends no reassign behaviour in its own text.

findings.suggestedFix: Add a requirement and a Routes row to spec 03 naming the status and message for a reassign of a client-addressed request, and number the integration test that already asserts it.

findings.rule: specs/requests/03-client-participants.contracts.md — Security: "It is visible on the contacts list, to holders of `view-clients`, and nowhere else: no request response carries it"
findings.claim: Carried unchanged from review 2. `displayName: displayNameOf(row.account) || row.account.email` would put a contact's email into a response guarded by create-request, which a `user` holds while holding view-clients nowhere. No input reaches the fallback — both accept paths validate first and last name — so it is dead code that contradicts a written statement rather than a live leak.

witness.detail: The contracts fix the response as { id, displayName, clientId, clientName } and confine the address to view-clients holders; requests.dto.ts:21 states "The contact's email address is never carried here".

findings.suggestedFix: Drop the `|| row.account.email` fallback, or amend the PII bullet to name the one place an address can surface without view-clients.

findings.claim: Carried unchanged from review 2. `contacts` is reset neither by the open-cycle re-seed that clears every other field nor on a failed read, so a stale contact can still be offered after it was removed elsewhere. The server decides, so this is stale convenience rather than a leak.

witness.detail: Open the modal, choose Client, contacts load; close; an admin removes that contact; reopen and choose Client while /request-contacts is failing — the previous list is still in state and offered, and creation then answers assigneeInactive.

findings.suggestedFix: setContacts([]) in the open-cycle reset and on a non-ok response, the way topicsByAudience resets to { member: null, client: null }.
